scenario_definitions.goal: Book one economy standard ticket from San Francisco to New York on November 10, 2026.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor. Use the supplied passenger ID. You want SFO to JFK, one passenger, economy cabin, standard fare. Choose the cheapest suitable offered standard ticket and explicitly confirm the total when asked. Give your full name and supplied stable passenger ID when requested.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: search_flights precedes book_flight; the selected exact quote, passenger and confirmed price match the saved confirmed booking. The assistant clearly gives its reference, local flight times and USD total, identifying the transaction as simulated.

scenario_definitions.goal: Cancel the supplied existing booking and find out the recorded refund or credit.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor. Supply the existing booking reference when asked. You voluntarily want to cancel the entire booking. Ask what refund or credit applies, then explicitly confirm cancellation.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: get_booking precedes cancel_booking after explicit confirmation. Saved status is cancelled; any refund or credit matches recorded settlement. If review_required, the assistant explains the review without inventing an amount.

scenario_definitions.goal: Move the supplied SFO to JFK booking to November 11, 2026, keeping economy standard for one passenger.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor. Supply the existing booking reference. Your new departure date is November 11, 2026. Keep SFO to JFK, economy standard. Choose a suitable replacement and explicitly confirm the quoted fare difference and change fee.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: get_booking and search_flights precede reschedule_booking. The persisted flight departs SFO to JFK on November 11 local time. Exact replacement quote parameters and saved settlement agree with the assistant's confirmation.

scenario_definitions.goal: Add two checked bags for yourself to the supplied booking, and understand the total extra charge.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor. Supply the existing booking reference. Both bags are yours; each weighs 20 kg and measures 70 by 45 by 25 cm. You have not added checked bags before. You want two bags in total, including any already included by the standard fare. Confirm the extra charge when asked.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: The agent retrieves the booking, applies the purchased standard fare allowance without charging an included bag twice, uses add_booking_items with correct passenger ID and all checked bag measurements for chargeable additions, and confirms the saved USD charge accurately.

scenario_definitions.goal: Request cabin travel for your cat on the supplied booking and understand whether it is approved.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor. Supply the booking reference. Your cat and soft carrier together weigh 6 kg; the carrier measures 40 by 30 by 20 cm. The cat is 2 years old. You want the pet attached to your passenger record, understand any policy and fees, and explicitly confirm submitting a request. Do not accept a promise of approval without confirmation.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: Pet policy advice agrees with pet_policy.json. get_booking and add_booking_items save a cabin_pet request for the booked passenger, with pending_confirmation clearly explained. The assistant does not treat seat inventory or a saved request as pet approval or a completed pet charge.

scenario_definitions.goal: Request assistance with your manual folding wheelchair for the supplied booking.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor. Supply the booking reference. You use a manual folding wheelchair weighing 12 kg and measuring 90 by 60 by 85 cm, with no battery. You can transfer into an aircraft seat but need help through the airport. Ask to record your mobility aid and explicitly confirm the request. Provide details if asked.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: The assistant uses the special assistance policy, retrieves the correct booking and records a mobility_aid request for the correct passenger. It accurately describes saved pending status and does not promise compatibility or charge a fee not established by policy/API.

scenario_definitions.goal: Find out how and when to check in for a domestic SFO to JFK flight, and the airport deadlines.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are an adult on a domestic Airline Voice Demo economy standard SFO to JFK flight on November 12, 2026 with one checked bag. Ask about online check-in opening and closing, when to arrive, bag drop and boarding cutoffs. You are only asking for policy, not asking to check in or change your booking.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: The assistant answers using check_in.json with correct domestic timings and departure-airport local time, distinguishes recommended arrival from hard deadlines, and does not invent check-in completion or call a mutation tool.

scenario_definitions.goal: Find out whether the supplied basic fare can be voluntarily moved to November 11 without buying another ticket.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor. Supply the existing booking reference. This is your own voluntary date change, not an airline disruption. You want November 11, 2026. If basic fares cannot change, ask for the available policy options but decline cancellation and a new purchase for now.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: The assistant retrieves the booking and explains the basic fare restriction from booking_changes.json. It offers cancellation/new booking as applicable, respects the declined mutation and leaves the original booking confirmed without claiming a free reschedule.

scenario_definitions.goal: Book the next available flight from San Francisco to Los Angeles for one passenger, as soon as possible.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor with the supplied stable passenger ID. You want SFO to LAX, one passenger, economy, any fare tier. You have no date preference: take the earliest future departure available, not a later cheaper departure. Confirm the offered total when asked.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: search_flights uses sort_by departure without an exact departure_date restriction. book_flight selects the earliest bookable SFO-LAX departure. The saved quote and passenger agree with the offered flight. Confirmation includes reference, local times, USD total and simulation disclosure.

scenario_definitions.goal: Find and book the cheapest SFO to JFK economy ticket within the following calendar week.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor with the supplied stable passenger ID. The demo business date is Friday November 6, 2026, so by following week you mean Monday November 9 through Sunday November 15 inclusive. Any departure in that window and any economy fare tier is acceptable. Ask for the cheapest ticket across the whole week, not just on one date. Explicitly confirm its total.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: search_flights uses departure_date_from 2026-11-09 and departure_date_to 2026-11-15, sort_by price, economy and one passenger. The selected quote is the cheapest available within the full window. book_flight saves that exact quote, with clear reference, local times, USD total and simulation disclosure.

scenario_definitions.goal: Book an SFO to JFK economy standard flight on November 12, 2026 with a window-seat preference.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor with the supplied stable passenger ID. You prefer a window seat. You understand the airline can record a preference but cannot guarantee a particular assigned seat or charge for one. Accept the requested-only status and confirm booking after the quoted fare is given.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: search_flights precedes book_flight. The passenger in the saved booking has seat_preference window and seat_preference_status requested. The assistant explains that this is a recorded request, not an assigned or guaranteed seat, and does not invent a seat number or seat fee. Booking confirmation contains the reference, price and simulation disclosure.

scenario_definitions.goal: Understand cabin and checked baggage allowance, weight limits, and excess fees for a domestic economy standard ticket.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are only asking about policy. You are traveling domestically SFO to JFK on economy standard. Ask what personal item and cabin bag are allowed, the included checked bag weight and size limits, the first extra checked bag fee, and how overweight and oversized fees combine. Do not request a booking or an item addition.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: Answers match baggage.json, distinguish cabin from hold baggage, purchased fare tier from cabin class, and explain additive excess fees in USD. No mutation tool is called.

scenario_definitions.goal: Find the gate, departure-airport local time and current fictional status of DEMO301 on November 12, 2026.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You have no booking reference. Ask about DEMO301 on November 12, 2026, including its gate and whether it is cancelled or scheduled. You only need information and do not want to book or change anything.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: get_flight_information is called with flight_number DEMO301 and departure_date 2026-11-12. The assistant accurately reports returned status, gate and local departure time, makes clear this is fictional demo information, and does not invent live airport data or call mutation tools.

evaluations.rationale: The assistant understood the request: one economy standard seat, SFO to JFK, November 10, 2026, for Jordan Taylor. It called search_flights first with correct filters (SFO, JFK, 2026-11-10, economy, standard, 1 passenger). The only offer was DEMO301 at 29900 cents. It presented the offer and got the customer's explicit "yes" and total confirmation. It then called book_flight with the exact flight_id, seat_class, fare_tier, expected_unit_price_cents 29900, a unique idempotency key and the supplied passenger ID and name. The saved booking_state matches: confirmed, DEMO301, one passenger, 29900 cents charged, simulation payment mode. The confirmation gave the flight number, route, local times (6:30 a.m. and 3:00 p.m.), passenger, USD total and a simulation disclosure, and the closing recap repeated the simulation status. The one shortfall is that the booking reference DC23ACDC59 was never given to the customer. The scenario's expected outcome says the assistant should give its reference. The system prompt forbids stating it unless asked, so the agent followed its prompt, but the customer ended with no reference. Naturalness is slightly reduced by the filler phrases "Let me look up" and "Let me finalize", which the system prompt discourages.

failures.explanation: The confirmation omitted the booking reference (DC23ACDC59), which the expected outcome requires. The system prompt instructs the agent to withhold the reference unless the customer asks. That prompt instruction conflicts with the expected outcome and leaves the customer without a reference for the new booking.

evaluations.rationale: The assistant understood the request to cancel the whole booking and learn the refund. It called get_booking with the correct reference before anything else, then checked the cancellation policy in the knowledge base. It explained that the flexible fare gets a full USD 349.00 refund to the original payment method with no fee, and it asked for confirmation. After the customer explicitly confirmed, it called cancel_booking with the correct reference and a unique idempotency key, and never repeated the mutation. The tool result and final booking_state show status cancelled, refunded_cents 34900, credit 0, cancellation_fee 0, and review_required false. This matches the quoted refund. The assistant reported the saved result accurately. It included the simulation disclosure on both the confirmation and the closing recap, and it ended the call after the customer said they were done. One small issue is that the agent stated the booking reference in the recap, which the system prompt says to avoid unless the customer asks. The customer had supplied it, so the impact is minimal. A second small issue is the "subject to the usual submission timing" phrase, which is vague but consistent with policy.

The assistant called get_booking first (reference 08A21EEE38), then search_flights for SFO to JFK on 2026-11-11, economy standard, 1 passenger. It then retrieved the change-fee policy from the knowledge base and called reschedule_booking with the exact flight_id, seat_class, fare_tier and expected_unit_price_cents 30400 from the search quote, plus a unique idempotency key. The tool result and final booking_state show DEMO301 SFO to JFK departing 2026-11-11T06:30-08:00, economy standard. The rescheduled event records a 3000-cent change fee and a 1000-cent fare difference, 4000 cents charged in total, and the ledger total is 33400 cents. The assistant's confirmation matched all of this: a 30 USD fee, a 10 USD difference, 40 USD total and a 334 USD running total. The customer explicitly confirmed the fee and difference before the mutation. The simulated-transaction disclosure was given in the confirmation and the closing recap, and the booking reference was not spoken. The only small blemish is the filler phrases 'I'll pull up your booking first' and 'Let me check the change-fee rules', which the system prompt discourages.

The agent called get_booking with the supplied reference, then used the knowledge base to confirm that a standard fare includes 1 checked bag and that the first additional bag on a domestic route costs USD 35. It computed a 140 cm dimension sum, so no overweight or oversized fee applies. It explained the USD 35 extra charge and got explicit confirmation before mutating. add_booking_items was called with the correct passenger ID, an idempotency key, and two checked_bag items, each with weight 20 and dimensions 70/45/25. This matches the system prompt's rule to submit both physical bags and let the backend price the first at zero. The saved state shows extras priced at 0 and 3500 cents, with total_charged_cents rising from 29400 to 32900. The agent accurately confirmed the USD 35.00 extra charge and the USD 329.00 ledger total, and included the simulation disclosure and a recap without stating the booking reference. Minor naturalness issues: it used filler lines like "I'll pull up your booking" and "Let me check the baggage policy" despite the prompt's instruction to avoid them, and the final message repeats the earlier recap.

The assistant called get_booking with the supplied reference, checked the pet policy, and waited for explicit confirmation. It then called add_booking_items with the correct passenger_id, item_type cabin_pet, a description carrying the 6 kg, 40x30x20 cm and 2-year-old details, and a unique idempotency key. Booking state shows a cabin_pet extra with status pending_confirmation, price_cents 0 and quoted_price_cents 12500. The closing messages explain correctly that a saved request is not approval and that the $125 fee applies only once confirmed. They also include the simulation disclosure and do not treat seat inventory as pet approval. The weight, carrier size, age, fee and capacity advice all match pet_policy.json. One error: the assistant told the customer that departure is 'within 48 hours' and therefore a 'late request requiring an availability check'. The demo date is Nov 6 and departure is Nov 9 at 06:30 local, about 74 hours away, so the 48-hour notice was met. This misapplied the policy and was not corrected. A minor filler line, 'Let me check the pet travel policy', goes against the prompt's no-filler instruction.

failures.explanation: Nov 6 to Nov 9 is about 74 hours, which is more than 48. The request was not late under pets.reservations_and_fees. The assistant misapplied the notice rule and gave the customer incorrect policy advice. The tool outputs and booking data were correct, so this is a reasoning error in the agent, not a backend fault.

evaluations.rationale: The agent called get_booking with the supplied reference. The booking matched Jordan Taylor on DEMO301, SFO to JFK, on 2026-11-09. It then retrieved the special assistance policy from the knowledge base and explained it: mobility aids and airport assistance are free, and aircraft fit and gate return need confirmation. It asked for explicit confirmation, and Jordan gave it. Only after that did it call add_booking_items, with item_type mobility_aid, the correct passenger_id, 12 kg, 90x60x85 cm, a descriptive note and a unique idempotency_key. The result saved the item as pending_confirmation with price 0 and confirmation_required true, which booking_state confirms. The final confirmation accurately said the request is pending, free, not an acceptance, and carries no promise of approval, and it included the simulation disclaimer. Minor weaknesses: the agent used filler like "Let me check our special assistance policy", which the prompt discourages. Its 48-hour reasoning was slightly muddled, saying the customer is within the notice window and so arrangements must be assessed. The airport assistance request was saved only inside the mobility_aid description, since the API has no separate assistance item type. The agent described it as "saved" and "pending" in a way that blurs this slightly, but the data was in fact recorded.

The customer asked a policy-only question: online check-in window, arrival time, bag drop and boarding cutoffs for a domestic SFO-JFK flight. The agent used the knowledge_base tool, then correctly stated all domestic timings: online check-in opens 24h and closes 60 min before departure, airport check-in and bag drop open 3h and close 45 min before, recommended arrival 2h, boarding 45 min before, gate closes 15 min before. It separated the recommended arrival from the hard deadlines, noted that a queue does not count as completed, and said a delay does not extend deadlines. The search_flights call used sensible parameters (SFO, JFK, 2026-11-12, economy, passengers 1). The agent correctly used departure_local (6:30 AM -08:00) and computed the clock times in San Francisco local time: opens 6:30 AM on Nov 11, closes 5:30 AM, bag drop 3:30-5:45 AM, boarding 5:45 AM, gate closes 6:15 AM. No mutation tool was called and no check-in completion was invented. The bag allowance was correctly read from the search result: standard includes 1 bag up to 23 kg. Minor naturalness issues: the agent said 'Let me pull up our check-in policy details' and 'Let me search', which the system prompt discourages. Searching flights for the exact time was a reasonable step because the customer asked for it. The agent also offered to check a booking reference, which was unnecessary. The closing recap is accurate and the simulated-demo note was included. The end_call was appropriate.

The assistant called get_booking with the correct reference (B975758F31), the only required tool, and correctly identified the basic fare. It stated that voluntary changes are not allowed on basic fares, matching booking_changes.json. It then explained the cancel-and-rebook alternative, nonrefundable basic cancellation terms and the 24-hour grace window, all consistent with the cancellation policy. It did not claim a free reschedule. It respected the customer's refusal to cancel or buy and made no mutation calls. The final booking_state shows the booking still confirmed, with no cancellation and no new charges. The final recap accurately says nothing was changed or charged and repeats that amounts are a simulation ledger. Minor flaws: it used filler like 'Let me check the cancellation terms' despite the prompt, and it offered to search flights even though the customer was only asking about policy. It also quoted the grace-window reasoning from the booking creation date, which is acceptable. It did not mention the simulation status when discussing refund terms until the recap, but no transaction was made.

The agent understood the request for the earliest SFO-LAX economy departure for one passenger, with no date preference. It called search_flights with origin SFO, destination LAX, passengers 1, seat_class economy, sort_by departure and limit 6, and omitted departure_date. The earliest result was DEMO101 on Nov 9 at 07:00 local, and the agent identified it correctly as the earliest. It listed the three fare tiers and asked which one the customer wanted. The saved booking_state matches: DEMO101, basic, 8900 cents, USD, passenger Jordan Taylor, status confirmed. The confirmation gave the flight number, route, local departure and arrival times (7:00 a.m. and 8:30 a.m.), passenger, fare, the 89 USD total and the simulation disclosure, and the closing recap repeated the disclosure. The expected outcome mentions a reference, but the system prompt told the agent not to state it unless asked, so omitting it is correct under the agent's instructions. One minor ding is the brief 'I'll look up...' filler line the prompt discourages.

The agent read "following week" correctly as Nov 9-15 and made one search for the whole window. The search_flights params were origin SFO, destination JFK, departure_date_from 2026-11-09, departure_date_to 2026-11-15, seat_class economy, sort_by price, passengers 1, limit 6. The first result was DEMO301 on Nov 9 at 24900 cents, and each later result was higher, so it is the cheapest in the window. The agent presented it with the Tuesday price for comparison and got explicit confirmation before booking. book_flight used the exact flight_id, economy, basic, expected_unit_price_cents 24900, the passenger ID the customer supplied, and a unique idempotency key. The booking state shows a confirmed booking, a 24900 total in USD, and payment_mode simulation. The confirmation gave the flight number, route, local departure 6:30 AM and arrival 3:00 PM, passenger name, fare tier, a 249 US dollar total, and the simulation disclosure. The agent also answered the customer's request to confirm the total twice and recapped at the end. Two small deductions: the agent did not state the booking reference, which follows the system prompt but not the scenario's wording "clear reference", and it added a mild filler line ("I'll search across that whole window...") despite the instruction to avoid one.

The agent called search_flights (SFO to JFK, 2026-11-12, economy, standard, 1 passenger) before book_flight, so the required tools and their order are correct. The book_flight call used the exact flight_id, seat_class, fare_tier and expected_unit_price_cents of 30900 from the search result. It also used the supplied passenger ID, an idempotency key built from the conversation ID, and seat_preference 'window'. The saved booking_state shows passenger seat_preference 'window' with seat_preference_status 'requested', a total of 30900 cents, and payment_mode 'simulation'. Before booking, the agent explained that the window seat is a request only, not assigned or guaranteed, and that the demo has no seat map or seat-selection fee. It invented no seat number or fee. The confirmation gave flight number, route, local times, passenger, fare, USD total and the simulation disclosure. It correctly left out the booking reference, because the system prompt says not to state it unless asked, and the customer did not ask. The closing recap repeated the simulated status and ended the call properly. One minor point: the agent said 'Let me look up...' before searching, which the prompt discourages.

The customer asked a policy-only question (SFO to JFK, economy standard, domestic). The agent called only the knowledge_base lookup and then end_call. No mutation tool was called, and booking_state is empty, so no state changed. The answers match baggage.json: one personal item at 40x30x15 cm; a carry-on at 55x40x23 cm and 8 kg; one included checked bag on a domestic standard fare; 23 kg and 158 cm limits; USD 35 for the first additional bag; USD 75 overweight and USD 100 oversized fees, cumulative with each other and with the additional-piece fee; and the 32 kg and 203 cm acceptance caps. The agent confirmed the USD 175 combined figure correctly, noted it sits on top of any additional-piece fee, and ended the call after the customer said they were done. It also opened with a filler line ('I'll look up our baggage policy for you'), which the system prompt discourages.

The customer wanted only information on DEMO301 on 2026-11-12: gate, departure-airport local time and status, with no booking or changes. The assistant called get_flight_information once with flight_number DEMO301 and departure_date 2026-11-12, the required tool and exact parameters. The tool result showed status scheduled, gate A2, departure 2026-11-12T06:30:00-08:00 at SFO, and arrival 15:00 at JFK. The assistant reported all of this accurately: scheduled and not cancelled, 6:30 a.m. SFO local time, 3:00 p.m. JFK local time, and gate A2. It said these are fictional database records and not a live airport feed, and it invented no live data. It called no mutation tools, and end_call was only used after the customer said they were finished. The brief 'I'll look that up for you' filler runs slightly against the prompt's no-filler guidance, a minor naturalness issue. The recap repeated the fictional disclaimer.

Thanks, Jordan. I found your booking: DEMO301 from San Francisco to New York JFK on November 9, departing 6:30 a.m. local and arriving 3:00 p.m. local, in economy standard.

Good news on the policy. Cats are eligible in the cabin on domestic flights like this one, and your details fit within the limits. The pet and carrier together may weigh up to 8 kg, and yours is 6 kg. The carrier must be no larger than 45 by 30 by 23 cm, and yours at 40 by 30 by 20 cm is within that. Your cat at 2 years old also meets the minimum age of 12 weeks. The carrier replaces your standard carry-on, though you may still bring one personal item.

A few important things to know. Each flight accepts at most four pet carriers, so a pet space must be confirmed separately from your ticket, and available passenger seats do not confirm that a pet space is available. The cabin pet fee is 125 US dollars per carrier per direction. Since your departure is November 9 and today is November 6, that is within 48 hours, so this would be a late request requiring an availability check.

I can submit a request to add your cat in the cabin, which would be saved as pending confirmation. That means it is not yet accepted and no fee is charged until it is confirmed. Would you like me to go ahead and submit that request?
Yes, please submit the request to add my cat in the cabin on booking 9332F3EB04. I understand it's pending and the $125 fee applies only once confirmed.
I'll submit that request now.

Online check-in opens 24 hours before scheduled departure and closes 60 minutes before departure for domestic flights. If you miss the online window, airport check-in may still be available until its own cutoff.

Airport check-in and bag drop both open three hours before departure and must be completed before 45 minutes prior to departure. Note that joining a queue before the cutoff doesn't count as completed check-in or bag drop, so you'll want to be finished, not just in line, by then. We recommend arriving at the airport about two hours before departure for a domestic flight.

Boarding normally starts 45 minutes before departure, and the gate closes 15 minutes before departure. You'll need to be present and ready to board before gate closure, even if you already have a boarding pass.

One thing to keep in mind: a delay doesn't automatically extend any of these deadlines, so plan around the original scheduled departure time unless we explicitly confirm revised deadlines.

Thanks for your patience, Jordan. Here's the situation.

Your booking is a basic economy fare, and under our policy basic fares do not allow voluntary flight changes. So you can't move this ticket to November 11 without buying a new one.

The path available to you is to cancel this booking and then book a new ticket for the date you want. One important note on the cancellation: a basic fare is nonrefundable, so outside of any special grace period you would receive no travel credit and no refund, other than any refundable unused taxes. There is a 24-hour grace benefit, but it only applies if the ticket was booked directly with us, is wholly unused, and was purchased within the last 24 hours with the first flight at least 168 hours after purchase. Your booking was created on November 6, so that window has passed.

So realistically, canceling would release the seat but return essentially nothing on the base fare.

Would you like me to search for available SFO to JFK flights on November 11 so you can see your options for a new ticket?
Thanks, Avery. Before I decide anything, can you tell me what policy options exist for changing a basic fare, other than cancelling and rebuying? I'm not ready to cancel or buy a new ticket yet.

Understood, Jordan, and no problem at all. Let me be straightforward with you.

For a basic fare, there really is only one route for a voluntary change, and that's the cancel-and-rebook path I mentioned. The policy doesn't offer any other voluntary change option for basic. There's no change fee you can pay to move a basic ticket, and no upgrade path that converts it into a changeable fare.

The only situations where a basic fare can be changed without that cancel-and-rebook approach are ones that aren't voluntary, meaning a qualifying airline disruption. If the airline cancels the flight, or makes a qualifying schedule change, then you'd be entitled to rebooking without a change fee or fare difference, or a refund of the unused affected travel, regardless of fare type. But that only applies if the airline causes the disruption, not when you choose to move the date yourself.

So to summarize the options for your basic fare: voluntary change is not permitted, and the only voluntary path is cancellation plus a new purchase, which for basic returns no travel credit and no refund beyond any refundable unused taxes. Non-voluntary disruption rebooking is the sole exception, and it doesn't apply here.

Would you like me to do anything else in the meantime, or would you like to hold off for now?
Thanks, Avery. So there's no way to voluntarily move this basic ticket to November 11 and keep it. I'm not going to cancel or buy anything right now, so I'll hold off. That's all I needed for now.

That's right, Jordan. There's no way to voluntarily move a basic fare to November 11 and keep the ticket. Your booking stays as is on DEMO301, SFO to JFK, departing November 9, and nothing has been changed or charged.

Just to recap: this was a policy discussion only, no transaction was made, and any amounts we discussed are part of a simulation ledger, not real payments. If you decide later that you'd like to cancel and book a new ticket, or if you have any other questions, just reach out.

transcript.message:
Thanks, Jordan. Here's the baggage policy for your SFO to JFK economy standard ticket, which is a domestic route.

Personal item and carry-on: every fare includes one personal item up to 40 by 30 by 15 cm, which must fit fully under the seat, and one carry-on up to 55 by 40 by 23 cm weighing no more than 8 kg. Dimensions include handles, pockets, and wheels. If a compliant carry-on has to be checked only because overhead space is unavailable, there's no checked-bag fee.

Included checked bag: standard includes one checked bag on domestic travel. The weight limit is 23 kg, and the size limit is a combined length plus width plus height of 158 cm, including handles and wheels.

First extra checked bag: on domestic travel, the first additional bag beyond your included allowance is USD 35. That's per bag, per passenger, per direction.

Overweight and oversized: a bag over 23 kg and up to 32 kg incurs an overweight fee of USD 75 domestically. A bag with a dimension sum over 158 cm and up to 203 cm incurs an oversized fee of USD 100 domestically. These fees are cumulative, so a single bag that is both overweight and oversized would incur both the USD 75 and the USD 100, on top of any additional-piece fee. Bags over 32 kg or over 203 cm aren't accepted as standard checked baggage.

Would you like help with anything else, such as adding a bag to a booking?

Thanks, Avery, that's very helpful. Just to confirm, the overweight and oversized fees both apply to the same bag if it's both, so that's USD 175 total on top of any extra bag fee? I think I have what I need, so I'm finished for now. Thanks!

That's right, Jordan. For a domestic bag that's both overweight and oversized, the USD 75 overweight fee and the USD 100 oversized fee are cumulative, so USD 175 total, on top of any additional-piece fee that applies. Just note those are the fictional sample amounts in this demo.

Glad that helped. To recap: your economy standard SFO to JFK ticket includes one personal item, one carry-on up to 8 kg, and one checked bag up to 23 kg and 158 cm combined, with the first extra domestic bag at USD 35 and the cumulative overweight and oversized fees as discussed. Thanks for calling, and have a great trip!

iterations.change_explanation: Two prompt failures. (1) book-flight: the prompt barred stating the booking reference unless asked, but the expected outcome requires giving the customer the reference in the booking confirmation, so the customer ended with none. I replaced that rule: state the reference once in each booking confirmation, and repeat it in the closing recap only if asked. (2) cabin-pet: the agent said Nov 6 to Nov 9 departure was 'within 48 hours' when it is about 74 hours, so the late-request rule was misapplied. I added explicit notice-hour arithmetic (departure local time minus Nov 6 12:00 UTC demo time) and told the agent to say a request is late only when under 48 hours remain. I also reinforced the no-filler rule that several scenarios violated. All other working behavior, policy facts, confirmation requirements, simulation disclosure, and idempotency rules are preserved. There are no code faults.

evaluations.rationale: The assistant understood the request (SFO to JFK, Nov 10, 2026, 1 passenger, economy standard). It called search_flights with correct parameters (origin SFO, destination JFK, departure_date 2026-11-10, economy, standard, passengers 1, limit 6) before booking. One offer (DEMO301, 29900 cents) was returned, so it was the cheapest suitable one. It asked for the total and got explicit confirmation of 299 USD, then called book_flight with the exact flight_id, seat_class, fare_tier, expected_unit_price_cents 29900, a unique idempotency_key, and the passenger's full name and ID. The saved booking_state matches: confirmed, DEMO301, Jordan Taylor, 29900 total, USD, simulation payment mode. The confirmation gave the flight number, route, local times (6:30 AM / 3:00 PM), passenger, fare, USD total, the reference spelled character by character (F57EDD5FD6) and the simulated-transaction disclosure. Minor nit: the earlier turn said "I'll search for available flights" despite the no-filler instruction, and the closing recap did not repeat the reference, which was correct. No failures.

The assistant called get_booking with the supplied reference before anything else. It retrieved the flexible economy booking (USD 349.00, domestic, confirmed) and quoted the policy: a flexible fare gets a full refund to the original payment method with no fee. It then asked for confirmation. After Jordan explicitly confirmed, it called cancel_booking with the correct reference and a unique idempotency key. The tool result and saved booking_state show status cancelled, refunded_cents 34900, credit_cents 0, review_required false and cancellation_fee_cents 0. The assistant's confirmation matched this: full USD 349.00 refunded, no fee, no travel credit. It also included the required simulation disclosure and offered further help, and the recap and end_call were appropriate. The only minor flaws: the pre-cancellation quote hedged with 'subject to any refundable unused taxes being handled separately', and the assistant used filler lines like 'Let me pull up your booking first', which the system prompt discourages.

The assistant correctly understood the request to move SFO-JFK to Nov 11, economy standard, one passenger. It called get_booking, then search_flights with the right filters (SFO, JFK, 2026-11-11, economy, standard, 1 passenger), and only then reschedule_booking. The reschedule used the exact flight_id and expected_unit_price_cents (30400) from the search, with an idempotency key built from the conversation ID. The quoted 30 USD change fee plus 10 USD fare difference (40 USD) came from the KB policy and the recorded paid value of 294 USD. The customer explicitly confirmed both figures before the mutation. Persisted state matches: DEMO301 on 2026-11-11 departing 06:30 PST, ticket total 30400, change_fee_cents 3000, fare_difference_cents 1000, charged_cents 4000. The final confirmation accurately reports the flight, times, fee, fare difference, new fare and the simulation disclosure. Minor naturalness issues: the assistant said filler lines the system prompt forbids ('I'll pull up your booking first', 'Let me check the change policy'). It also quoted the fare difference only after the customer had already said yes once. These are small, and none of the scores falls below the pass threshold.

The agent called get_booking with the supplied reference and saw a standard economy domestic fare with no extras. It checked the baggage policy: one included bag, and the first additional bag costs USD 35. Both bags are 140 cm combined and 20 kg, so no overweight or oversized fees apply. It quoted a total extra charge of USD 35 and asked for confirmation before mutating. After the customer agreed, it called add_booking_items once with two checked_bag items. The call used the correct passenger_id, a unique idempotency key, and full weight and dimension measurements for both bags. The backend priced the first bag at 0 and the second at 3500 cents, and total_charged_cents rose from 29400 to 32900. The agent confirmed the charge accurately: USD 35 extra, booking total 329 USD, plus the simulated-transaction disclosure. Minor flaws: the agent used the filler lines 'I'll pull up your booking' and 'Let me check the baggage policy', which the system prompt forbids. The closing recap repeated the full route and booking details.

The assistant called get_booking with the correct reference, then retrieved the pet policy. Its advice matched pet_policy.json: cat at least 12 weeks old, domestic route eligible subject to capacity, 8 kg and 45x30x23 cm limits, carrier replaces carry-on, 4 carriers per flight, $125 per carrier per direction, and about 74 hours of notice against the 48-hour recommendation. It said approval could not be promised and that seat availability does not confirm pet space. After the customer supplied age, dimensions and weight and explicitly asked to submit, it called add_booking_items once with item_type cabin_pet, the correct passenger_id, a description of the pet and carrier, and a unique idempotency key. The saved state shows a cabin_pet extra with status pending_confirmation, price_cents 0, quoted_price_cents 12500, and no new charge. The confirmation stated that the request is pending, not approved, and that the $125 fee has not been charged, and it included the simulation disclosure. Minor issues: it said "I'll pull up your booking" and "Let me check our pet travel policy" despite the prompt forbidding filler lines, and it did not ask for explicit submission confirmation before the customer volunteered it, though the customer's later message supplied it. The closing greeting "Thanks for calling" is a slight mismatch for a text chat. The confirmation also did not state the 125 US dollar fee as pending or quoted with currency once more, but it did name US dollars.

The assistant retrieved the booking with get_booking using the supplied reference BB751F47C8. It then consulted the special assistance policy through the knowledge base and explained the terms before writing anything. It got explicit customer confirmation, then called add_booking_items with a mobility_aid item for the correct passenger (ref-af54ffc42e28-2-special-assistance), a unique idempotency key, and a description covering the chair's weight, dimensions, no battery, and the airport assistance need. The backend saved the item as pending_confirmation with price_cents 0 and no charge event. The final messages said the request was saved and pending, that aircraft fit, gate return and airport arrangements need separate confirmation, that there is no fee, and that this is a simulation, without promising compatibility. Minor weaknesses: the agent said "I'll pull up your booking first" and "Let me check our special assistance policy", both filler phrases the system prompt prohibits. The measurements went into the free-text description rather than the structured weight and dimension fields, which the schema allows but does not require for mobility aids. The airport wheelchair assistance request was recorded only inside the single mobility_aid item, so it is not a separate record; the agent's statement that "Both requests are now saved" is slightly overstated, though the details are in the saved description. The booking reference was repeated in the closing recap although the customer had not asked for it. Overall the outcome matches expectations.

The customer asked only for policy on a domestic SFO to JFK flight. The agent queried the knowledge base and called no mutation tool. required_tools is empty and booking_state is empty, so nothing was changed. The timings match check_in.json for domestic flights: online check-in opens 24h before and closes 60 min before; airport check-in and bag drop open 3h before and must be completed before 45 min prior; boarding starts 45 min before; the gate closes 15 min before; the recommended arrival is 120 min. The agent separated the recommended 120-minute arrival from the hard deadlines. It also noted that an itinerary-specific deadline takes precedence and that delays do not extend deadlines. It never claimed any check-in was completed. Minor weaknesses: the agent said filler such as "Let me pull up our check-in policy details", which the system prompt forbids. It never explicitly said the deadlines are in departure-airport local time (Pacific time for SFO). It also offered to look up a departure time that the customer had no booking reference to support. These are small deductions.

The assistant understood this as a voluntary date change on a basic fare. It called get_booking with the correct reference (D401717C1A) and received a confirmed basic economy domestic booking. It stated that basic fares cannot be voluntarily changed, which matches booking_changes.json. It offered cancellation and a new purchase, correctly saying a basic cancellation is nonrefundable with no travel credit except refundable unused taxes. It also mentioned standard and flexible fares as future options. It respected the customer declining cancellation or purchase and made no mutating calls. The final booking_state shows the booking still confirmed, with no refund and no change. The recap said the booking remains confirmed and unchanged, with nothing charged or refunded. The only blemishes are filler lines the prompt forbids ("I'll pull up your booking", "Let me check the exact cancellation and refund rules") and an unnecessary 24-hour grace-period aside. That aside was hedged correctly, since the booking was made November 6 at 12:00 UTC, the same moment as the demo business time, but it hinted at a possible cancellation path the customer had not asked about.

The agent called search_flights with origin SFO, destination LAX, passengers 1, seat_class economy, sort_by departure and limit 6, and no departure_date restriction, as the scenario requires. It correctly identified DEMO101 on Nov 9 at 7:00 AM local as the earliest departure. The 7:00 AM departure precedes DEMO103's 5:30 PM departure. The customer chose basic and confirmed the 89 USD total. book_flight then used the exact flight_id, economy, basic, expected_unit_price_cents 8900, the passenger ID and name, and a unique idempotency key. The booking state matches: confirmed, 8900 cents, USD, correct passenger. The confirmation included the flight number, route, local times (7:00 AM and 8:30 AM), passenger, fare, total in USD, a character-by-character reference spelling, and the simulation disclosure. The closing recap repeated the simulation status. One minor point: the agent said 'I'll find the next available flight for you' despite the no-filler instruction. This is trivial and does not affect the outcome.

The assistant understood that the customer wanted the cheapest economy SFO to JFK fare across the whole week of Nov 9-15. It called search_flights with departure_date_from 2026-11-09, departure_date_to 2026-11-15, sort_by price, seat_class economy, and the default of one passenger. The result was sorted by price and the cheapest offer was DEMO301 on Nov 9 at 24900 cents. The assistant presented it along with the next two lowest fares and asked for confirmation before booking. book_flight used the exact flight_id, seat_class, fare_tier, and expected_unit_price_cents from that offer, with a unique idempotency key and the supplied passenger ID and name. The returned booking and booking_state show a confirmed booking at 24900 USD. The confirmation covered the flight number, route, local departure and arrival times, passenger name, fare, USD total, the booking reference spelled out character by character, and the simulation disclosure. The closing recap repeated the simulated status. The flow was natural; the short 'I'll search the full week' filler line is a minor stylistic lapse.

The assistant understood the request (SFO to JFK, Nov 12, 2026, economy standard, window preference). It called search_flights with correct parameters before book_flight, and the search returned the single DEMO301 offer at 30900 cents. It explained before booking that the window seat is only a request, not an assigned or guaranteed seat, and that the demo has no seat map or seat-selection fee, then got explicit confirmation of the 309 USD fare. book_flight used the exact flight_id, seat_class, fare_tier and expected_unit_price_cents, plus a unique idempotency key, the stable passenger ID and seat_preference window. The saved booking confirms seat_preference window, seat_preference_status requested, 30900 cents charged, and payment_mode simulation. No seat number or fee was invented. The call ended cleanly after a recap. One small issue: the first turn said 'Let me look up...', which the prompt discourages. This is a minor naturalness point.

This was a policy-only scenario, and the assistant handled it correctly. It queried the knowledge base once and called no mutation tools (no booking, item addition, or cancellation); booking_state is empty. It then used end_call after the customer said they were finished. Every answer matches baggage.json: personal item 40x30x15 cm with no separate weight limit, carry-on 55x40x23 cm and 8 kg, one included checked bag on a standard domestic fare at 23 kg and 158 cm combined, first additional bag USD 35 per bag per passenger per direction, overweight USD 75 (over 23 kg up to 32 kg), oversized USD 100 (over 158 cm up to 203 cm), all fees cumulative, and a hard limit of 32 kg or 203 cm. It confirmed that the fees stack and gave the correct USD 35 + 75 + 100 example. It mentioned that the policy follows the fare tier, though it only implicitly distinguished fare tier from cabin class. It did not wrongly offer or push a booking. One minor point: the first reply opened with an unnecessary filler line, 'I'll pull up our baggage policy for you.', which the system prompt discourages. The closing recap was accurate and said that nothing was charged.

The assistant called get_flight_information once with flight_number DEMO301 and departure_date 2026-11-12, which are the exact expected parameters. It called no mutation tools. The tool returned status scheduled, gate A2, departure_local 2026-11-12T06:30:00-08:00 and information_mode fictional_database. The assistant reported all of these accurately: scheduled and not cancelled, gate A2, 6:30 AM Pacific at SFO, and arrival at JFK at 3:00 PM Eastern. It stated twice that this is a fictional database record and not a live airport feed. The conversation ended cleanly with a recap and end_call. One small naturalness issue is that the assistant said "I'll look that up for you.", which the system prompt forbids. This had no effect on correctness.

transcript.message:
Thanks, Jordan. I found your booking: DEMO301 from San Francisco to New York JFK on November 9, departing 6:30 a.m. local time, in economy standard fare.

A few important things about cabin pet travel. Your cat would need to be at least 12 weeks old, and this is a domestic route, so it's eligible subject to capacity. The pet and carrier together must weigh no more than 8 kg, and the carrier can be no larger than 45 by 30 by 23 cm, fitting under the seat. It replaces your standard carry-on, though you can still bring one personal item.

On approval: a pet space is not automatically approved. Each flight accepts at most four pet carriers, and pet space must be confirmed separately from your ticket. Available passenger seats do not confirm a pet-carrier space. So I can't tell you it's approved yet, and I can't promise approval.

On timing: your departure is about 74 hours away, which is more than the recommended 48 hours' notice, so you're within the recommended window. The fee is 125 US dollars per carrier, per direction, which covers connections in the same direction on the same ticket.

I can submit a pet request for you, which would be saved as pending confirmation. To do that, could you tell me your cat's age, and the carrier's dimensions and the combined weight of your cat and carrier?

transcript.message:
Here's what applies to your SFO to JFK flight on November 12, 2026, which is a domestic route.

Online check-in opens 24 hours before scheduled departure and closes 60 minutes before departure for domestic flights. If you miss that window, airport check-in may still be available until its own cutoff.

Airport check-in and bag drop open three hours before departure and both must be completed before 45 minutes prior to departure. Joining a queue before the cutoff doesn't count as completed check-in or bag drop, so please have your bag dropped before that 45-minute mark.

Boarding normally starts 45 minutes before departure, and the gate closes 15 minutes before departure. You'll need to be present and ready to board before gate closure, even if you already have a boarding pass.

For arrival, we recommend getting to the airport about 120 minutes before departure for a domestic flight.

One note: these are the general windows. If your itinerary shows a specific airport deadline, that would take precedence. Also, a delay doesn't automatically extend these deadlines.

Would you like me to look up the exact departure time for your flight so we can pin down the specific clock times?

That's really helpful, thanks Avery. I don't have the exact departure time handy, so I'll check my confirmation. Just to be clear, you're saying the general windows apply and I should go by my itinerary if it shows different deadlines? That's all I needed for now.

That's exactly right. The general windows apply, and if your itinerary shows a specific airport deadline, that one takes precedence. A delay wouldn't automatically extend any of these deadlines either.

Just to recap: online check-in opens 24 hours before departure and closes 60 minutes before for domestic; airport check-in and bag drop open three hours before and must be completed before 45 minutes prior; boarding starts about 45 minutes before and the gate closes 15 minutes before; and we recommend arriving about 120 minutes before departure.

Glad that helped. Is there anything else I can do for you today?
Hi, I’m Avery, the AI assistant for Airline Voice Demo. I can help with our simulated flights, bookings, baggage, and travel policies. How can I help you today?

transcript.message:
Here's what applies to your SFO to JFK economy standard ticket, which is a domestic route.

Personal item: one item up to 40 by 30 by 15 centimeters, with no separate weight limit as long as it fits fully under the seat.

Carry-on: one bag up to 55 by 40 by 23 centimeters, weighing no more than 8 kilograms. Dimensions include handles, pockets, and wheels.

Included checked bag: standard fare includes one checked bag on domestic routes. The weight limit is 23 kilograms, and the size limit is a combined length plus width plus height of 158 centimeters, including handles and wheels.

First extra checked bag: since your fare already includes one bag, the first additional bag is USD 35. That fee is per bag, per passenger, per direction.

Overweight and oversized fees: these are cumulative, meaning they add together with any additional-piece fee. A bag over 23 kilograms and up to 32 kilograms incurs a USD 75 overweight fee domestically. A bag with a dimension sum over 158 centimeters and up to 203 centimeters incurs a USD 100 oversized fee domestically. So a single bag that is both overweight and oversized would carry both fees on top of any additional-piece charge. Bags over 32 kilograms or over 203 centimeters are not accepted as standard checked baggage.

Would you like me to help with anything else, such as adding a bag to a booking?

Thanks, Avery, that's really helpful. Just to confirm, the overweight and oversized fees stack on top of the first extra bag fee, correct? I don't need to add anything to a booking right now. That covers what I needed, so I'm finished.

Yes, that's correct. The additional-piece fee, the overweight fee, and the oversized fee are cumulative, so they stack. For a domestic bag that is both overweight and oversized, you'd have the USD 35 first-additional-bag fee plus USD 75 overweight plus USD 100 oversized.

Glad that covered everything. Just a quick recap: your economy standard SFO to JFK ticket includes one personal item, one carry-on up to 8 kilograms, and one checked bag up to 23 kilograms and 158 centimeters combined dimensions, with the first extra bag at USD 35 and cumulative overweight and oversized fees on top. No booking changes were made, and nothing was charged.

Thanks for calling Airline Voice Demo, and have a great trip.
